text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- State may need to recapitalise state-owned electronics group Thomson SA to balance the negative effects of its 25 billion franc debt before privatisation. Successful bidder -- Alcatel Alsthom and Matra submitted bids as expcted on Monday -- will be known in early October.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe presents a 1997 budget on Wednesday which, barring surprises, will target a 1997 deficit at the high end of the 270 to 280 billion franc range.
-- Glass group Saint-Gobain strengthens its activity in the United States.
-- French and German Finance Ministers meet at Kempten, Germany, today over monetary pact for 1999.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Credit Agricole increases its share in Suez to over five percent.

-- Budget deficit was 8 billion francs smaller at the end of July than a year before, but this contributes little to the 35-billion-francs deficit reduction planned by the government for this year. A further freeze on spending may be implemented.

-- President Jacques Chirac unenthusiastic about the need for a law on work hours reduction. But expresses support for businesses at a CNPF employers' anniversary celebration, drawing back from his earlier criticisms.
-- Saint-Gobain to invest three billion francs in glass firms in the United States.
L'AGEFI
-- Financial markets appear confident over the 1997 budget proposals to be presented tonmorrow.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Real-estate association chairman calls for government incentive scheme to help real-estate buyers, modelled on automobile incentives.
-- Public works group Eiffage posts a 890-million-franc loss for the first half.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Ailing appliance manufacturer Moulinex plans to shed jobs in France, hires in new Mexico plant.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- France begins to scrap its land-based missiles
